format: Unsigned native x86 PE32 GUI, MSVC C++, statically linked SQLite 3.45.1; no appended archive or packed secondary payload identified.
method: Complete cleave facts, PE headers/imports/sections, objdump disassembly, Rizin function and cross-reference analysis, and analytical reconstruction of encrypted constants. The executable was not launched and no embedded endpoint was contacted.

hopper_prior_evidence.note: Stored sandbox score >=8/10. The disposition is independently supported by the code review; the sandbox score was not treated as proof.

reverse_engineering.startup_and_cover: The program exposes JournalTrace - Event Trace Viewer v4.2.1 UI strings and synthetic event messages. The main routine compares its normalized executable name with securityhealthservice.exe; that branch hides the console and calls the collection routine at 0x443c20, then 0x448030. Another call into collection occurs at 0x4046ae.
reverse_engineering.persistence: Collection immediately calls 0x44a700. This obtains the executable's own path, constructs an AppData destination ending in SecurityHealthService.exe, creates the directory, copies itself with CopyFileA at 0x44aa28, opens HKCU Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run at 0x44ab08, and writes the startup value with RegSetValueExA at 0x44abad.
reverse_engineering.browser_passwords: The collection routine directly calls 0x442a70 to recover an encrypted_key from browser Local State and uses the dynamically resolved DPAPI/CNG functions. It directly calls 0x438d50, which reconstructs SELECT origin_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins at 0x43956e. 0x439f30 reconstructs SELECT name, value FROM autofill at 0x43a594. Browser profile enumeration and local database reads surround these operations.
reverse_engineering.discord: The binary contains both normal-token and dQw4w9WgXcQ encrypted-token search expressions, Local Storage/leveldb targets, Discord client variants, Local State/encrypted_key processing, and DPAPI/AES-GCM helpers. The collection routine builds a Discord Tokens report before passing it to the common sender.
reverse_engineering.network_sender: 0x446ba0 reconstructs CryptUnprotectData, BCrypt cryptography APIs, and the WinHTTP API table before resolving them through LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress. 0x434ed0 is called directly from collection with generated report bodies and builds Telegram requests. 0x41a520 contains GDI desktop capture using GetDC, BitBlt(SRCCOPY) and GetDIBits, multipart octet-stream framing, api.telegram.org and /sendDocument, and WinHTTP calls. A call to this capture/sender routine is present at 0x449295.
reverse_engineering.destination: A Telegram bot token and recipient identifier are embedded in encrypted form. They are retained only in the temporary forensic artifacts and are not detection gates.
reverse_engineering.encryption: String decoder functions derive a byte keystream from s = seed + index*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo 2^64, followed by xor-shifts left 13, right 7, left 17, then XOR its low byte with the ciphertext. Equivalent vector and scalar paths are present. Multiple constant arrays and decoder callers were decoded and cross-checked manually; no emulated OS calls were needed.
reverse_engineering.limits: Static analysis establishes the implemented collection, persistence and send paths. It does not establish that a particular victim's credentials were successfully decrypted or delivered. No specific malware-family attribution is made.

detection_repairs.encoded_references: Six neutral observations recover the encoded DPAPI API prefix, WinHTTP send API prefix, Telegram hostname/document-method prefix, browser credential SQL prefix, and Run-key prefix. They follow the relative decoder call and stack-source LEA, read the variable seed from its decoder, and verify the decoded bytes mathematically. No sample hash, name, bot token, fixed address or fixed seed is required.
detection_repairs.boundaries: Encoded-code observations require an executable PE section and bind the caller's stack-source operand to the ciphertext's first store. Supported layouts are EBP disp8, EBP disp32, ESP disp8 and EBP stores crossing the disp8 boundary. Rules are scoped to x86 PE/DLL files smaller than 16 MiB, with 768-byte caller/decoder windows. Prefix observations are named explicitly and do not claim an API call or credential transfer alone.
detection_repairs.discord_formats: Accept source-escaped backslashes and a 24-to-26 first token segment. Extend the neutral paired-format observation to native PE/DLL. The shared prefix observation preserves source-text handling and directly scans binary bytes because the binary-string extractor filtered this sample's high-entropy marker.
detection_repairs.engine_limit: The installed engine limits YARA matches per pattern to eight during evaluation. The encoded-reference matchers use boolean call anchors and bounded direct byte reads instead of indexed match arrays, so a real witness after many decoys remains detectable. No engine source or scanner retention limit was changed.
detection_repairs.hostile_composites: Browser theft, Discord theft and Telegram credential-sender composites require distinct credential-source, local-key decryption, encoded destination/operation, HTTP sender and dynamic API-resolution evidence. Their descriptions state static co-occurrence rather than observed transfer. The Run-key/self-copy/API conjunction remains suspicious because legitimate startup software remains possible without the credential-theft context.

verification.control_coverage: Different random seeds, all four stack layouts, more than eight preceding decoys, missing source/decryption/sender roles, legitimate bot and credential-tool cases, wrong source LEA, wrong relative call, non-executable data and absent GetProcAddress import.
